issue.title: Core-floor gates check binding names but not wire schema versions, so a schema bump can ship with a floor that rejects it at runtime
issue.description:
Discovered by sase-k2.land while landing epic sase-k2 on 2026-08-12 (workspace sase_13, HEAD 67d846327). The immediate breakage was fixed as part of that landing; this bead is for the missing gate that let it through.

WHAT HAPPENED: phase sase-k2.5 bumped src/sase/core/external_pr_wire.py's EXTERNAL_PR_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION from 1 to 2 and landed the matching Rust classifier in sase-core (fb3c869), first published as sase-core-rs 0.26.5. Two minutes later, an unrelated epic's commit 688eec2bd ratcheted pyproject.toml to 'sase-core-rs>=0.26.4,<0.27.0' with uv.lock resolved to exactly 0.26.4. sase-core 0.26.4 ships EXTERNAL_PR_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1 (crates/sase_core/src/external_pr/wire.rs) and classify.rs:36 rejects any other value. Any environment resolving from the lockfile rather than building against a linked sase-core checkout would therefore have failed every external_pr_mirror pass with a schema-mismatch error — src/sase/core/rust.py is deliberately strict and has no Python fallback. sase-k2.land raised the floor to >=0.26.5 and refreshed the lock.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: tools/probe_core_floor diagnoses staleness from the collected core BINDING-NAME set (_collect_binding_names, tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings). plan_external_pr_import exists in 0.26.4, so name presence passes. tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version only compares version numbers against the pyproject specifier. Neither gate knows that a shared wire-schema constant has a required minimum, so a floor can satisfy both while being semantically too old.

SCOPE: give the floor gates a notion of required wire-schema version. Options: have the probe read Python's *_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION constants and compare them against the same constants in the floor version's published wheel; or add a cheap runtime assertion/test that round-trips each wire schema through the installed binding so a too-old floor fails a gate rather than a chop. Worth covering every wire schema, not just external-PR: grep '_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION' under src/sase/core/.

SECOND, SEPARATE OBSERVATION (reproduced, recorded here rather than filed twice): 'python3 tools/probe_core_floor --advisory' under this machine's default python3 (3.11.13 via pyenv) exits with status could_not_determine — 'could not collect core binding names: type _HostedResolverFactory = Callable[ ... SyntaxError: invalid syntax' — because it parses PEP 695 'type X = ...' aliases with a pre-3.12 interpreter. Under .venv/bin/python it runs clean. So the probe is blind rather than wrong when invoked with the wrong interpreter. sase-jj's close reason called out this exact symptom and explicitly invited filing it separately.

RELEVANT FILES: tools/probe_core_floor, tools/validate_sase_core_rs_version, tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings, tools/ratchet_core_window, src/sase/core/external_pr_wire.py, src/sase/core/rust.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-jj — the fifth-instance stale-core-floor bead, closed 2026-08-12. Its close reason established that 90912ad7d moved floor-window ownership to the release-branch ratchet, and separately recorded the probe_core_floor could_not_determine/PEP 695 symptom this bead reproduces. This bead is the distinct remaining gap: the ratchet fired, but to a version older than the wire schema the tree had just started requiring.

evidence.note:
Independent second instance from epic sase-k3, found by sase-k3.land, with a WORSE failure mode than the external-PR case: silent degradation instead of a loud schema-mismatch error.

Phase sase-k3.4 (commit 8f9c5c3ff, 13:52) added 'freshness' to the agent-scan artifact-index query wire (src/sase/core/agent_scan_wire_records.py, sent at src/sase/core/agent_scan_wire_conversion.py). The Rust side landed in sase-core 61cc793 and first shipped in sase-core-rs 0.26.5 (release commit d2a418d bumps Cargo.toml 0.26.4 -> 0.26.5, despite its 'release v0.26.4' subject). Exactly like the external-PR case, commit 688eec2bd had already pinned the floor to '>=0.26.4,<0.27.0' with uv.lock at 0.26.4, 21 minutes before sase-k3.4 landed -- so the same window was open for this wire too.

THE DIFFERENCE THAT MATTERS FOR YOUR SCOPE: AgentArtifactIndexQueryWire.freshness is declared '#[serde(default)]' with Default = Revalidate (crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/index.rs:83), and the struct has no deny_unknown_fields. On 0.26.4 the field simply does not exist, so serde drops it silently and every ACE startup query falls back to full revalidation. No error, no chop failure, no test failure -- just the silent loss of the largest single win in epic sase-k3 (Tier-1 loader query 1.861s revalidate vs 0.280-0.464s cached, measured on athena at 1f388edee).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMEDIATION: the 'cheap runtime assertion that round-trips each wire schema through the installed binding' option in this bead's scope would NOT catch this instance -- a round-trip succeeds on 0.26.4 because the unknown field is silently dropped and the response still deserializes. Catching serde-default field additions needs field-presence checking against the floor version's published wheel (the first option in your scope), or a behavioral assertion that the cached mode actually skips revalidation. Worth widening the scope note beyond '*_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION' constants: this wire never bumped a schema version at all, so grepping for that constant would have missed it entirely.

ALREADY REMEDIATED, NOT STILL BROKEN: origin/master commit b4c6038e6 raised the floor to '>=0.26.5,<0.27.0', which covers this wire as well as the external-PR one. Recording it here because it doubles the evidence for the missing gate and narrows which fix would actually work.
